headline: PLS.AX slumps 4.7% to drag the ASX lower, while TTWO surged nearly 5% last night on GTA VI hype — and the RBA held rates steady, giving mortgage holders a breather.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a rough session today, dropping 4.7% to $5.88. The broader ASX sold off sharply (down 1.5%), and lithium stocks were caught in the downdraft. Despite some positive longer-term noise about AI data centres lifting battery demand, the near-term sentiment on lithium remains weak — Pilbara is still down nearly 13% on your total investment.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a strong session last night, jumping almost 5% to $239.28. GTA VI hype is running hot — there's talk of an $80 price tag and a third trailer dropping when pre-orders open. A streamer reportedly offered $250,000 for early access. Market enthusiasm around the game's release is clearly building, and the stock is now up 4.3% on your total investment.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google had a solid session last night, up 1.48% to $367.46. The tailwinds are real — AI spending momentum, ongoing cloud growth, and reported Berkshire Hathaway interest in the stock are all keeping sentiment positive. You're up nearly 20% on this position.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.74% today in a broadly weak ASX session. Emerging markets ETFs are sensitive to global risk sentiment, and with the ASX down 1.5% today there wasn't much shelter here. Virtually break-even on the overall position.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.56% today, mostly dragged down by the weak ASX session. As a diversified fund with exposure to both Aussie and global equities, it tends to move with the broader market. Still up about 1.9% on your total investment.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.61% today to $8.10. Crude oil (WTI) barely moved — down just 0.08% to $76.54 — so this was more a case of the overall ASX weakness pulling it down rather than any specific energy news.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.22% today to $18.16 — a small positive in an otherwise soft ASX session, which reflects steady AI sector sentiment. Still down about 3.85% on your total investment though.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today, up just 0.07% to $525.46. As a US market ETF trading on the ASX, it tracked last night's muted US session. Up nearly 2% on your total investment — solid and steady.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft barely moved last night, up just 0.13% to $379.40. The stock is in a holding pattern ahead of earnings — analysts are watching AI strategy execution and cloud revenue closely. You're still down about 14% on this position, though the long-term AI story remains intact.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Sharp 4.7% drop today — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell 4.7% today to $5.88, its worst session in a while, dragged down by the broader ASX sell-off. The long-term lithium demand story (especially AI data centre battery demand) is still intact, but short-term sentiment is rough. You're down 12.76% on this position. Don't panic sell into weakness, but watch for any further deterioration.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI hype fuelling big gains — hold and watch
watch_today.detail: Take-Two surged 4.93% last night to $239.28 and is now up 4.3% on your total investment. GTA VI pre-order buzz is building — analysts expect an $80 price point and a third trailer to drop with pre-orders. The stock could keep running as a release date gets closer, but it's also priced for perfection. Hold and enjoy the ride, but be ready for volatility.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Earnings on the horizon — hold and watch closely
watch_today.detail: Microsoft was almost flat last night (+0.13%), but earnings are coming up and the market will be watching AI strategy and cloud revenue hard. You're down 14.38% on this position — a strong earnings beat could start to close that gap. Keep this one on your radar this week.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — good news for mortgage holders and growth stocks
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank left interest rates unchanged this week, giving Aussie mortgage holders a reprieve. Lower-for-longer rates are generally good for growth-oriented ETFs like VDHG and tech stocks. Nothing to act on immediately, but it's a mild tailwind for your portfolio.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 fell 1.53% today — broader market weakness
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 dropped 137 points to 8,828 today — a meaningful sell-off that hit most of your ASX holdings. Gold also slid 1.2% to $4,172/oz. Keep an eye on whether US markets follow suit tonight when they open at 11:30 PM AEST.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Strong momentum — consider topping up on any dip
watch_today.detail: Google is up 1.48% last night to $367.46 and you're sitting on a 19.5% gain. AI spending momentum, cloud growth, and reported Berkshire interest are all tailwinds. Your position is small (only 0.23 shares / ~$119 AUD). If US markets pull back tonight and GOOG dips, it could be a decent entry point to add to this winner.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Sunday session, closing down 1.53% to 8,828 — one of its sharper single-day falls recently. On the commodity front, gold dropped 1.2% to around $4,173/oz while crude oil was basically flat at $76.54. The Aussie dollar held steady at 70.16 US cents. US markets (S&P 500 and NASDAQ) don't have fresh data yet — they open tonight at 11:30 PM AEST.

politics.summary: The big domestic news this week is the RBA holding interest rates steady — a relief for millions of Aussie mortgage holders. AI regulation is also heating up globally, which has implications for Australian tech policy down the track.

stories.title: RBA Leaves Interest Rates on Hold — Relief for Aussie Borrowers
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia decided to leave interest rates unchanged at its June meeting. For anyone with a mortgage, this means no increase to repayments — welcome news after a prolonged period of rate hikes. It also signals that the RBA thinks inflation is under enough control that it doesn't need to keep tightening. Markets had been hoping for this outcome, and it's a mild positive for growth-oriented investments like equities.

ai.summary: The dominant AI story globally right now is regulation — governments, media companies, and international bodies are all grappling with how to manage AI. There's no single breakthrough product story this week, but the regulatory momentum is worth watching as it will shape how companies like Google and Microsoft operate.

stories.title: French President Urges US to Share Cutting-Edge AI — and Calls for Democratic Nations to Cooperate on Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: French President Macron called on the United States to share its most advanced AI technology with allied democracies, and urged Western nations to build a coordinated regulatory framework rather than each country going it alone. The concern is that if democracies don't align on AI rules, authoritarian states could gain a technological edge. For investors, this signals that big AI companies like Google and Microsoft may face more international oversight — but a coordinated Western framework could also actually reduce regulatory fragmentation and uncertainty.

stories.title: As Calls for AI Regulation Grow, Media Faces a Defining Moment
stories.why_it_matters: Media organisations are under increasing pressure to adapt as AI tools get better at generating content, summarising news, and replacing traditional search traffic. The industry is at a fork in the road: either embrace AI partnerships (like some publishers have done with Google and OpenAI) or fight for stricter content licensing rules. This matters for Alphabet (GOOG) as content licensing disputes with news publishers could become a regulatory and cost headache.

stories.title: Have the G7 Effectively Regulated Generative AI for Children's Safety Online?
stories.why_it_matters: A University of Sheffield analysis questions whether G7 nations have actually done enough to protect minors from generative AI tools — things like AI chatbots, image generators, and deepfakes. The research suggests current frameworks are patchy and inconsistent across countries. This is increasingly a hot-button political issue in Australia too, following the social media age restrictions debate, and could lead to tighter rules on AI platforms.

stories.title: Get Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini in a Single Lifetime AI Platform for Under $70
stories.why_it_matters: A new bundled platform is offering lifetime access to Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), and Gemini (Google) for a one-off payment of under $70 USD. In practical terms, this means you can run queries across all three major AI assistants from one interface — useful for comparing answers or using each for different tasks. It's a sign of how commoditised AI assistant access is becoming, which is both an opportunity and a pricing pressure for the big players.

sport.summary: Big NRL weekend with the Titans pulling off a home upset over Penrith and the Warriors demolishing the Cowboys in Auckland. AFL icon Tony Modra is recovering after major surgery following a serious car crash. Round 16 wrapping up with Storm vs Raiders in the second half as we speak.

stories.title: Titans Stun Penrith 19-18 at Cbus Super Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans pulled off a one-point upset over the reigning-dynasty Panthers at home on Saturday, winning 19-18. This is a big result for the Titans in their own backyard — Penrith have been one of the competition's powerhouses and any win over them is significant. Great news for local fans on the Gold Coast heading into the second half of the season.

stories.title: Warriors 38 Cowboys 20 — But Serious Injury Cloud Over Star Blues Hopeful
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors steamrolled the Cowboys 38-20 in Auckland in a dominant performance, but the win was overshadowed by a serious injury to a player described as a Blues State of Origin hopeful. The nature and timeline of the injury weren't fully confirmed at time of writing, but concern was high in the Warriors camp. A big result on the field, but potentially a painful blow for their squad depth.

stories.title: Dolphins Make It Seven Wins in a Row, Beating Injury-Ravaged Tigers 36-22
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins are on a seven-game winning streak after beating the Tigers 36-22 in Campbelltown. The Tigers were short-handed due to injuries, making it a somewhat comfortable win for the Dolphins — but seven in a row is seven in a row. They're building serious momentum in the second half of the season and looking like genuine finals contenders.

stories.title: AFL Icon Tony Modra 'Stable' and on the Mend After Major Surgery
stories.why_it_matters: AFL legend Tony Modra — famous for his spectacular marking and goal-kicking in the 90s — is recovering in hospital after major surgery following a serious car crash. Reports from 7NEWS say he is stable and on the mend, though he'll carry 'battle scars' from the incident. The AFL community was widely shaken by the news, with players and fans rallying around him on social media. Good signs that he's on the road to recovery.
